nodes.summary: A closed straight-line system is acyclic when every defining term mentions only earlier variables, and the query mentions only defined variables. Hence every variable occurring anywhere in the system is defined, and unfolding the definitions terminates at ground terms: there is no free input variable.
nodes.title: Acyclic closed straight-line system

nodes.summary: The decision procedure checks the query on the unique ground assignment; it does not search over free inputs, because the closed fragment has none.
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a closed acyclic straight-line system is decidable

nodes.summary: Any satisfying assignment agrees with the candidate on defined variables.
nodes.title: Satisfying assignments agree with the candidate on defined variables

nodes.summary: Satisfiability of a closed straight-line system is equivalent to the query holding on the candidate assignment.
nodes.title: Straight-line satisfiability iff the query holds on the candidate

nodes.summary: The defining equation for the folded values: the value at position `acc.length + k` is the `k`-th defining term evaluated under the folded values. The variable condition says the term only looks at positions below `acc.length + k`.
nodes.title: Defining equation for the folded values

nodes.summary: The fold appends exactly one value per definition.
nodes.title: Straight-line fold appends one value per definition

nodes.summary: The fold preserves its initial segment.
nodes.title: Straight-line fold preserves its initial segment

nodes.summary: Lookup in an appended list agrees with lookup below the prefix length.
nodes.title: Lookup in an appended list below the prefix length

nodes.summary: Lookup with a proof of the bound is the `getElem` value.
nodes.title: In-bounds lookup with default equals indexed access

nodes.summary: Lookup in a folded list agrees with lookup in the starting list below its length.
nodes.title: Lookup in a folded list below the starting length

nodes.summary: Lookup in a taken prefix agrees with lookup in the whole list.
nodes.title: Lookup in a taken prefix agrees with the whole list

nodes.summary: One fold step: evaluate the next defining term under the values computed so far and append the result.
nodes.title: One fold step of straight-line evaluation

nodes.summary: Satisfaction of a closed straight-line system: the assignment obeys every definition and satisfies the query.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a closed straight-line system

nodes.summary: A closed straight-line system: one defining term per variable, plus a query formula. The definition at position `k` is the definition of variable `k`. There are no free input variables: every variable the system talks about must be defined by the system itself.
nodes.title: Closed straight-line system

nodes.summary: The candidate assignment satisfies every definition.
nodes.title: Candidate assignment satisfies every definition

nodes.summary: The candidate assignment of a straight-line system.
nodes.title: Candidate assignment of a straight-line system

nodes.summary: Length of the folded values: one per definition.
nodes.title: Folded values have one entry per definition

nodes.summary: The folded assignment values, in variable order.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
